# Citation

Peng, B., and Kimmel, M. (2005). *simuPOP: a forward-time population genetics simulation environment*. Bioinformatics. DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bti584. Source: [https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/21/18/3686/202296](https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/21/18/3686/202296).

# One-Sentence Summary

Introduces simuPOP, a forward-time population-genetics framework with configurable genotype structures, operators, population subdivision, selection, and mating schemes.

# Scope for simitall

Use as the cited engine behind the optional Python bridge. simitall remains responsible for R-facing validation, workflow design, provenance, and R-native outputs.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- A population can include subpopulations, explicit loci, ploidy, chromosome positions, and individual information fields.
- Evolution is composed from initialization, pre-mating, mating, post-mating, and final operators.
- Built-in mating schemes include random mating, selfing, monogamy, polygamy, cloning, and controlled allele-frequency trajectories.

# Inputs to Specify

- Genotype structure and locus positions
- Population or subpopulation sizes
- Mating, mutation, migration, selection, and recombination operators

# Expected Outputs

- Evolved genotypes
- Individual and family metadata
- Pedigree-compatible ancestry information when configured

# Limitations and Guardrails

- A simulation engine does not make a parameterization biologically realistic by itself.
- Users must choose map positions, founder variation, demography, and selection assumptions deliberately.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- Which simuPOP mating preset matches an F2, selfing, or random-mating design?
- How should an R workflow pass loci and recombination information to simuPOP?
